title: Divided authority: the operator signs off at gates, and only there
situation: The operator, 2026-10-16, signed off the read-back of the sign-off-gates story. A fresh architect asked to read a change back before recording read back, then recorded on the shared line of work in the same turn and handed the work to a lead: the design gave the operator no right between stating intent and release, its read-back was an ordering only, and the architect's decisiveness had no bound. The operator added that the gate and the sign-off are two things, the point and the right exercised there.
decision: (1) The operator and the architect stand in a client engagement with divided authority, each sovereign in its own domain. The operator decides intent, priority and release and holds sign-off, exercised at the gates and only there: a story's read-back (the architect's), a story's plan read-back (the lead's; a task with no story skips it unless the operator calls it), a pull request the operator reviews (the lead's, before it merges), release, a fork that is irreversible, about value or beyond the architect's competence, and any gate the operator calls, stop included. (2) A story starts only when the operator signs off its read-back; nothing else counts as being told to start. (3) A gate is held in the session of the party whose handover it is, whose turn ends there until the operator answers; the operator joins that session, and the delegating party learns only that it waits, then the result, so technical colour reaches the lead and never passes through the architect. Pushing a branch or opening a pull request is never a gate; between gates the agents work without checking in. (4) The architect decides meaning only and rectifies every input, the operator's included, restating it in established names and reading the restatement back where it differs; it disagrees with reasons, and a requirement the operator states, once understood, binds. How a story is split into tasks and how many builders it takes is the lead's. (5) The operator may grant delegated authority over a scope, naming the sign-offs taken in its place, the limits it keeps and an end state; its read-back comes once, at the end state.
consequences: The decision rights, operator, architect, lead, read-back, gate, sign-off, delegated authority and intent-based delegation concepts state this. The architect's and lead's agents are bounded to it in the sign-off-gates story.
